post.summary: Focus the terminal session of a running agent in its session wrapper.
post.description:
The web UI's launch panel calls this for **cmux** launches: cmux exposes no
browser URL scheme, so the operator control plane (which runs inside cmux)
shells out to `cmux focus-workspace` for the agent's saved workspace ref to
bring its pane to the foreground. Other wrappers are unsupported here - VS
Code focuses through its extension's URI handler, and tmux/zellij are
display-only in the UI, so it never calls this for them.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: The agent ID whose session to focus

parameters.name: x-operator-csrf
parameters.description: Required for cookie-authenticated mutations; omit when using bearer authentication.

400.description: Wrapper unsupported, or no session refs to focus

get.summary: Get an issue type's Operator workflow document
get.description:
Returns the issue type verbatim, in the same shape as the `<KEY>.json` files
in a hosted collection bundle (`/schemas/issuetype.json`). This is the
*native* Operator workflow - the ordered step graph every export format is
derived from - so the web UI and the docs site render identical graphs from
identical bytes. Prefer [`get_one`] for display metadata; use this when you
need the full step structure including step types, reject edges, and
per-type fan-out configuration.

AgentProfile.description:
A canonical cross-tool agent definition (serialized as `agent-profile.json`).

Shared core (`name`/`provider`/`model`/`system_prompt`/`skills`/`mcp_servers`/
`tools`) plus namespaced extension bags. `x_operator` is typed (Operator owns
those fields); `x_agnt` and `x_openai` are opaque per-platform pass-throughs.

mcp_servers.description: MCP server names. Preserved opaquely across import.

oneOf.description: Declarative reference to a remote, named agent. `None` = a locally launchable agent, not bound to a remote target.

skills.description: Named skills. Preserved opaquely across import.

system_prompt.description: System prompt. This is preserved opaquely across import (see [`Delegator::unmapped_core`]).

tools.description: Tool names. Preserved opaquely across import.

x_openai.description: OpenAI-owned extension fields, opaque (`instructions`, `tools`, `tool_resources`, `metadata`, thread refs, ...).

oneOf.description: Operator-owned extension fields (typed). `None` when the agent carries no Operator-specific configuration.

AssessTicketResponse.description: Response from creating an ASSESS ticket

ticket_path.description: Path to the created ticket file

BootstrapState.description: Where the deployment sits in the one-time admin-creation sequence.

BootstrapStatusResponse.description:
Current bootstrap state, readable without authentication so a client can
route a first-time visitor to setup rather than to login.

requires_temporary_password.description:
Whether a temporary password was supplied out of band (a mounted
bootstrap secret). When true, submission must present it.

state.description: The state this deployment is in.

BootstrapSubmitRequest.description: Claim the admin account and set its password.

new_password.description: The admin password to set. Never persisted in plaintext or logged.

temporary_password.description:
The out-of-band temporary password, when
`requires_temporary_password` is set. Never persisted or logged.

state.description: The state after submission - `Complete` on success.

username.description: The account name created by bootstrap.

created.description: ISO-8601 date the collection was first published.

icon_path.description: Bare filename of the collection's SVG icon, next to its manifest.

updated.description: ISO-8601 date of the last substantive revision.

url.description: Link to the collection's source repository or project page.

oneOf.description: Descriptive workflow hints (present for hosted collections).

ConfigurationResponse.description: The deliberately supported, integration-safe configuration surface.

CreateAccessKeyRequest.description: Create a service access key for an integration.

expires_in_days.description:
Days until the key expires. Expiry is mandatory - there is no
non-expiring key.

name.description: Human-readable label identifying what holds this key.

scopes.description: Scopes to grant. Only what the integration needs.

CreateAccessKeyResponse.description:
A newly created access key. **The secret appears here and nowhere else,
ever** - only its hash is stored, so it cannot be shown again.

secret.description: The key secret, returned exactly once. Store it now; it is unrecoverable.

DelegatorLaunchConfig.description:
Launch configuration for a delegator

Controls how the delegator launches agents. Optional fields use tri-state
semantics: `None` = inherit from global config, `Some(true/false)` = override.

create_branch.description: Whether to create a git branch for the ticket (None = default behavior)

docker.description:
DEPRECATED: prefer `target`. Run in docker container
(None = fall back to `launch.docker.enabled`, then local).

host.description:
DEPRECATED: prefer `target`. Name of a declared `RemoteHost` (from
`Config.hosts`) to launch the agent CLI on over SSH. `None` = local.

operator_relay.description: Override global relay auto-inject MCP setting per-delegator (None = use global setting)

prompt_prefix.description: Prompt text to prepend before the generated step prompt

prompt_suffix.description: Prompt text to append after the generated step prompt

target.description:
Name of an execution target: an explicit `[[targets]]` entry, the
synthesized `local`/`docker` targets, or a `[[hosts]]` name.
Supersedes `docker` and `host`.

use_worktrees.description: Override global `git.use_worktrees` per-delegator (None = use global setting)

DelegatorLaunchConfigDto.description:
Launch configuration DTO for delegators

Optional fields use tri-state semantics: `None` = inherit global config,
`Some(true/false)` = explicit override per-delegator.

create_branch.description: Whether to create a git branch for the ticket (None = default behavior)

docker.description: Run in docker container (None = use global `launch.docker.enabled`)

host.description:
Name of a declared `RemoteHost` to launch the agent CLI on over SSH (None = local).
DEPRECATED: prefer `target`.

operator_relay.description: Override global relay auto-inject MCP setting per-delegator (None = use global setting)

prompt_prefix.description: Prompt text to prepend before the generated step prompt

prompt_suffix.description: Prompt text to append after the generated step prompt

target.description:
Name of an execution target (explicit `[[targets]]` entry, synthesized
`local`/`docker`, or a `[[hosts]]` name). Supersedes `docker`/`host`.

drift between surfaces.

KanbanStatusMapping.description:

external board's column/status names.

Drives bidirectional sync: issues are pulled from the `todo` column,
pushed to `doing` when a ticket is claimed, to `done` when completed, and
back to `todo` when requeued. Unset fields fall back per-transition
(`doing` → "In Progress", `done` → "Done"); requeue only pushes when
`todo` is explicitly mapped.

todo.description: External column for operator "todo" (queued work; also the pull source)

skipped.description: Ticket IDs that were skipped (already exist)

filename.description:

for co-located clients; remote clients treat tickets as API-only)

status.description: Current status: queued, running, awaiting, completed

ticket_type.description: Ticket type: FEAT, FIX, INV, SPIKE

delegator.description: Named delegator to use (takes precedence over provider/model)

docker/coder/ssh orchestration is server-side); `command` is then
empty and the client must NOT run anything.

agents are API/memory-native and live on the remote side; Operator has no
runtime client for them, so a delegator carrying one is **export-only** and
cannot be launched locally (see the guard in `delegator_resolution`).

Scope.description:
A typed authorization scope.

Scopes are **not hierarchical**: `Write` does not imply `Read`. A credential
is granted each scope it needs explicitly, so an integration's authority is
legible from its scope list alone rather than requiring the reader to reason
about implication.

Lets clients rebuild the tree (e.g. LLM tools → model aliases).

Stable, section-scoped row id. Clients use it as a tree key and to route
row-specific commands without matching on the (mutable) display label.
Dynamic rows carry their entity key (issue-type key, project name);
static rows carry a fixed slug (e.g. "git-token").
